text.p: Libertel, the Netherlands' second digital mobile phone operator, said on Tuesday it was planning to offer per-second billing from October 1 as a way of stepping up growth in the Dutch mobile phone market.
Libertel, launched at the end of September last year, is 52 percent owned by Dutch financial group ING and 35 percent by U.K. mobile phone operator Vodafone Plc.

"This move is all about market development," Libertel managing director John de Wit told a news conference. "If we ever want to get to 25 percent market penetration we're not going to do it with the pricing of yesterday."
De Wit told reporters that Libertel had 140,000 subscribers, up from 120,000 in July, and reiterated a previous forecast that the company would have 200,000 by the end of the year.
He said mobile telephone penetration in the Netherlands was due to top six percent of the population by the end of the year, double that at the beginning of 1996.

Per-second billing means subscribers pay only for the airtime they use instead of having to pay by the unit, giving Libertel a potential competitive edge against the previous monopoly mobile and fixed telecoms provider Koninklijke PTT Nederland (Dutch PTT).
De Wit said the move would have no impact on Libertel's revenues as continuing strong growth in subscriber numbers would smooth out any dip in sales from the billing change.
"Our revenue will grow every month. We won't have a dip in our revenue stream because of this, because our growing curve is that steep," he said.

De Wit told the news conference that Libertel was planning to bring out fresh services and tariffs targeting clients' future needs, hinting at new combinations of fixed and mobile telephony without giving any details.
